RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 25

The panel's gender composition alone is not evidence of bias. Selection panels typically reflect specific institutional roles or committee appointments rather than personal preference. Raising the panel's demographics directly will likely be viewed as unfounded and could harm your professional standing.

Although your administrative qualifications appear stronger on paper, principal appointments depend heavily on interview evaluations, strategic vision, school fit, and references. 

Instead, send a polite follow-up requesting the written feedback you were promised. If their explanation reveals procedural flaws, shifting criteria, or clear bias, consult your union representative or an employment lawyer. Base any formal inquiry strictly on objective selection criteria and procedure, not the personal characteristics of the panel members.
